issue: The Ollama embed() function (POST /api/embeddings, same model bge-m3, same error handling) is copy-pasted in 6 files across rag/ and the search-docs MCP server. The Qdrant client construction, COLLECTION constant, buildFilter() and snippet() helpers are likewise duplicated between rag/query.ts and mcp/search-docs/src/index.ts. There is no shared retrieval/embedding module.
evidence: async function embed(text){ fetch(`${OLLAMA_URL}/api/embeddings`, {... model: OLLAMA_MODEL, prompt: text ...}) } repeated verbatim in rag/query.ts, rag/ingest.ts, rag/hybrid.ts, rag/hybrid-rerank.ts, rag/ingest-hybrid.ts, mcp/search-docs/src/index.ts
recommendation: Extract a single rag/lib/embeddings.ts (embed, OLLAMA_URL/MODEL) and rag/lib/qdrant.ts (client, buildFilter, snippet, PointPayload) module; have both the RAG CLIs and the search-docs MCP server import them. Pin one canonical default for QDRANT_URL/OLLAMA_URL/COLLECTION there. Cross-ref PERF-07 (process spawn) lives next to the same boundary.

issue: The search-docs MCP server — the production/served retrieval interface that AGENTS.md mandates agents use FIRST — is hardwired to the dense-only collection 'proshop_docs' (plain qdrant.search). The hybrid (dense+sparse RRF) and hybrid+cross-encoder-rerank pipelines, which are the better-quality retrieval design, exist only as standalone rag/hybrid.ts / rag/hybrid-rerank.ts CLIs against a DIFFERENT collection 'proshop_docs_hybrid'. The best retrieval path is unreachable from the interface that is actually consumed.
evidence: search-docs: COLLECTION ?? 'proshop_docs'; qdrant.search(...).  hybrid.ts: COLLECTION='proshop_docs_hybrid'; client.query(... prefetch dense+sparse, fusion rrf ...)
recommendation: Decide the canonical retrieval design and document it as an ADR (see Proposed ADR-0004). Route the MCP server through the chosen pipeline (hybrid or hybrid+rerank) and the chosen collection so served quality matches the experimental quality, or explicitly document why the MCP stays dense-only.

issue: The feature-flags admin UI is implemented TWICE with two contradictory state patterns. DashboardFeaturesScreen.js uses the ADR-0002 Redux/thunk path (featureFlagActions + featureFlagListReducer, registered in store.js). admin/FeatureFlagsScreen.jsx uses a parallel useFeatures.js hook doing raw fetch('/api/feature-flags') into local useState, bypassing Redux entirely. Both are wired as live routes (/admin/features and /admin/feature-flags).
evidence: useFeatures.js: fetch('/api/feature-flags').then(...) + useState; store.js registers featureFlagList reducer used by the OTHER screen
adr_quote: New cross-screen state, API-backed workflow state, and persistence-sensitive UI flows should default to this model unless there is a clear reason to keep them local to a single component tree.
recommendation: Pick one feature-flags screen as canonical. If the Redux path is canonical (per ADR-0002), delete useFeatures.js + admin/FeatureFlagsScreen.jsx (or vice-versa) and remove the dead route. If the local-fetch hook is intentional, record the exception explicitly.

issue: features.json has two independent owners with no shared schema or access module. The Express controller (read-only) and the feature-flags MCP server (read+write, owns the canonical Feature TypeScript interface, the atomic tmp+rename write, the Status enum, traffic-canonicalisation and dependency-warning rules) each re-implement readFeatures()/JSON.parse against the same file. The contract (field names, status vocabulary, traffic invariants) lives in the MCP server only; the backend duplicates the read path and the entry-shaping (toEntry vs {feature_id,...feature}) with no shared definition.
evidence: featureFlagController.js: readFeatures = async()=>JSON.parse(await readFile(FEATURES_PATH)).  index.ts: readFlags + writeFlags(atomic) + Feature interface + canonicalTrafficForState
recommendation: Introduce a single feature-flags access module (shared package or a backend service that the controller and MCP both consume) that owns the schema, validation, read, and atomic write. At minimum publish the Feature/Status contract once. See Proposed ADR-0005 for the file-as-store decision itself.

issue: server.js (the composition root / wiring layer) contains an inline route handler with business logic: app.get('/api/config/paypal', (req,res)=>res.send(process.env.PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID)). This bypasses the routes->controller->(service) convention every other endpoint follows (AGENTS.md 'Conventions'). Separately, featureFlagController does direct filesystem I/O (readFile + JSON.parse of features.json) inside the controller, business/persistence logic that the layering convention places in a service/model layer; the backend has no service layer for non-Mongoose persistence so file access leaks into the controller.
evidence: server.js:33 inline handler reading process.env; featureFlagController.js:10 await readFile(FEATURES_PATH,'utf-8')
recommendation: Move the paypal config endpoint into a controller mounted via a route (e.g. configController.getPaypalClientId). Extract features.json access into a featureFlagService / shared module (see ARCH-04) so controllers orchestrate and the persistence detail (file read, atomic write) sits behind an abstraction.

issue: Service-endpoint defaults diverge across the retrieval stack with no central config. search-docs MCP defaults QDRANT_URL/OLLAMA_URL to 'http://localhost:...' while every rag/*.ts file defaults to 'http://127.0.0.1:...'. On hosts where localhost and 127.0.0.1 resolve differently (IPv6 ::1, container networking) the MCP server and the ingest job can talk to different endpoints. There is also no docker-compose service for qdrant/ollama/mcp/rag, so the orchestrated topology (ADR-0001 'simple production topology') silently excludes these self-built services.
evidence: search-docs: 'http://localhost:6333' vs rag: 'http://127.0.0.1:6333'; docker-compose.yml has only mongo/backend/frontend
recommendation: Centralise QDRANT_URL/OLLAMA_URL/COLLECTION defaults in one shared config (resolves with ARCH-01) and pick a single literal. Document where the RAG/MCP/Qdrant/Ollama services run relative to ADR-0001's topology, or add them to docker-compose.

issue: Controller JSDoc route annotations contradict the actual mounted HTTP verbs and access levels: updateOrderToPaid is annotated '@route GET /api/orders/:id/pay' but mounted as PUT; updateOrderToDelivered annotated 'GET' but mounted PUT. The feature-flags endpoints are annotated '@access Public' which is accurate but contradicts ADR-0003's principle of enforcing access at the route boundary (cross-ref SEC-04 — these read routes are unauthenticated). The annotations are the closest thing to an API contract and they have drifted.
evidence: // @route GET /api/orders/:id/pay  above a handler mounted via router.route('/:id/pay').put(...)
adr_quote: New protected endpoints should compose the existing middleware model by default.
recommendation: Fix the JSDoc verbs to match routes. Decide whether feature-flags reads should be protected per ADR-0003 (cross-ref SEC-04) and either add protect/admin or document the public exception.

issue: ADR-0001/0002/0003 compliance baseline (positive). ADR-0001: split MERN holds — Express serves /api/*, /uploads, and frontend/build in production (server.js:38-45), frontend uses relative /api paths. ADR-0003: JWT bearer + protect/admin middleware is composed correctly at the route boundary in orderRoutes/userRoutes (no inline authz in those controllers). ADR-0002: Redux+thunk+localStorage store is intact in store.js. The architectural deviations from these ADRs are captured in ARCH-02..ARCH-07; the MCP/RAG subsystems are entirely undocumented by any ADR (see Proposed ADR-0004/0005).
recommendation: Keep ADR-0001/0002/0003 as the baseline; add ADR-0004 (RAG/Qdrant retrieval design) and ADR-0005 (feature-flags-as-JSON-file with MCP write ownership) to cover the undocumented self-built subsystems.
